Hi [~accountid:6075604653cc020069760c71] ,

Really appreciate that you’re allocating some time from your schedule during closing. I’ve one observation on the demo. On the first day, employee is being allocated a pro-rated allowance, when they have spend just 4 hours in travel during that particular day. Our allowed rate should only be given when any employee at least spend *5 hours or more* (25% of daily rate). 

So for first day, employee should not get any allowance. The allowance for 2nd and 3rd day looks fine, also the meal adjustment is ok. I see on the 3rd day, employee is getting 75% of the daily rate (adjusted by meals allowed), because they’ve already spend 10 hours. So this is correct and as per our expectations. Employee should not get 75% if they’ve not spend 10 hours or more in a day.

*Warm Regards,*
Subarna

Hi all! As discussed with [~accountid:6172754ef485cd006863a3a8] and [~accountid:62134a797580350068337097] we have a problem with UA and AZ. In the T&Cs with the partners (restaurants), the partners grant respective UA/AZ local entity the licence to use the menu, however, this licence is without the right to grant a sublicence - this means that legally, UA/AZ entity is not allowed to give Bolt Operations or Invisible the right to use the menu. Meaning that if we do it, we are breaching the T&Cs. We want to resolve this issue with our next global T&Cs update planned in Decemeber 2023. Hence, there are two options how to proceed:
1. We will sign agreements with Invisible for UA and AZ later this year, once we have new T&Cs in place in UA and AZ which allow local entity to grant sublicence - this would legally be the correct way to proceed.

2. We will sign agreements with Invisible for UA and AZ immediately - we will be breaching the T&Cs, however, from what I understood from [~accountid:62134a797580350068337097] we have been cooperating with Invisible in UA and AZ for already two years so we have been breading the T&Cs for two years anyways. We consider the risk for loss for restaurants low if we breach the T&Cs, however, it’s the business decision which way we will go and how urgent is the signing of the agreements. It is not up to the legal team to decide.

*(2) In addition, under the conditions laid down in paragraph 1 (1), the prosecuting authority or the court may order that:*

*(a) any individual or legal person on the territory of Romania to communicate computer data, in his possession or under his control, which are stored in a computer system or on a computer storage medium;*
*(b) any service provider providing services in the territory of Romania to communicate data in its possession or control relating to subscribers, users and such services.”* and as per article 271 alin. 1(Obstruction of justice):”*(1) A person who, having been warned of the consequences of his act:*

*(a) unlawfully prevents the prosecuting authority or the court from carrying out a procedural act in accordance with the law;*

*(b) refuses to make available to the prosecuting authority, the court or the court judge, in whole or in part, data, information, documents or property in his possession which he has been expressly requested to provide, in accordance with the law, for the purpose of the resolution of a case, shall be punished by imprisonment for a term of three months to one year or by a fine.*”

We would like to follow up on not including supervisory board members and Ahto Kink as a management board member.

As per IAS 23 par 9, ‘key management personnel’ includes “any director (whether executive or otherwise)”. 

As per the definition of key management personnel, all directors (whether executive or otherwise) of the entity are presumed to have the authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the entity and are therefore considered as key management personnel of the entity. The term ‘or otherwise’ is intended to cover non-executive directors and supervisory board members, as well as those who have responsibility for the management and direction of a significant part of the business without holding the title ‘director’.

In case in your view this does not apply for Bolt, please share a more detailed analysis indicating why Supervisory board members do not have any opportunity to for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the entity.

In case of Ahto Kink being Management board member, in our view it is even more unlikely he may not be considered a key management personnel, as as per Estonian legislation he may represent the Company on his own in all transactions. 

We can agree with limiting the close family members as per your suggestion, although we will require an explicit statement from your side to the fact that no other family members of the agreed related parties can influence the decision process.

Further, please also share a list of entities controlled by key management personnel, as these are also considered related parties.

[~accountid:712020:435d7fc1-7078-4aa9-b2a5-32758f7e11e4] I reviewed the DPA. Please find my comments below:

Clause 5.2 '*Subcontracting*' - CarValoo states that they are entitled to use subcontractors without the prior written consent of the Controller (Bolt). It does not align with Bolt's internal policies and procedures. Our internal procedure is approved by our Leadership Team and allows us to retain the right of prior approval of sub-processors. Any limitation to prior specific written authorisation will considerably delay the execution of this agreement, as we will have to seek internal approval.

Clause 5.2.1 - two weeks notice is not enough. It should be 30 day notice period or 20 days as a final position.

Clause 5.3. - I do not fully understand this clause. If it relates to liability then we cannot accept it. Article 28(4) of the GDPR requires the Processor to "remain fully liable to the controller for the performance" of its sub-processors obligations where that sub-processor fails to fulfil its data protection obligations. The GDPR does not provide any exceptions or caveats to this obligation.

Clause 6.7 '*Audit*' - Processor wants the costs of the audit to be borne by Bolt. We cannot accept this clause. The regulatory requirement stemming from Article 28(3)(h) of the GDPR imposes an obligation (to be included in contract) for the Processor to make available all information necessary to demonstrate compliance and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Controller.

Clause 7 '*Notification in Case of Data Violations by Processor*' - The Processor shall notify Bolt within "24 hours" after discovery of a Personal Data Breach. In order for Bolt to be able to comply with its direct obligations to, for example, notify supervisory authorities of a Personal Data Breach within 72 hours, Bolt requires the Processor to provide within 24 hours at the latest.

Clause 11 '*Liability*' - this section conflicts with our DPA approach.

I would advise to push for our own DPA template. If we don't get anywhere, we can look at theirs and amend accordingly. I will share our DPA template shortly.

h3. *Reasons*

This occurs for all orders that require 3DS. If payment method is ApplePay or GooglePay, Payments always require 3DS: 
[https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/625ae76e4381f461fe955a3d48b936f1e5a3b930/src/platform/payment/payment_provider_processout/main/controller/PaymentControllerGooglepay.ts#L140|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/625ae76e4381f461fe955a3d48b936f1e5a3b930/src/platform/payment/payment_provider_processout/main/controller/PaymentControllerGooglepay.ts#L140]
[https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/625ae76e4381f461fe955a3d48b936f1e5a3b930/src/platform/payment/payment_provider_processout/main/controller/PaymentControllerApplepay.ts#L199|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/625ae76e4381f461fe955a3d48b936f1e5a3b930/src/platform/payment/payment_provider_processout/main/controller/PaymentControllerApplepay.ts#L199]

For Rides the behaviour is as follows:

* client calls {{/client/v1/createRide/}}
* order is created
* flow goes to Commerce
* *Fraud is called for the first time*
* then {{ride-commerce}} gets response from Payments, asking for challenge ({{PAYMENT_PROCESSOUT_CHALLENGE_APPLEPAY}} for Applepay, {{PROCESSOUT_CHALLENGE_GOOGLEPAY}} for GooglePay)
* *client again calls* {{/client/v1/createRide/}}
* flow again goes to Commerce
* *Fraud is called for the 2nd time*
* I assume that now Commerce knows that challenge is passed, so the second call succeeds and the order is progressing further

h3. *Possible solutions*

There is a ticket on the client app side: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CLIENTAPP-25513|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/CLIENTAPP-25513|smart-link]. In the comments Alexey Kazakovskiy suggests that *the problem will be fixed after releasing “Order waiting state“*. 

However, it depends on how Rides will call Commerce. Also, this new feature is available for Rides, but we have problems also for MM. I suggest to wait for this feature and re-check after that, if the problem still occurs.

Additional answers to your questions (For Elina/Kristjan) 🙂 

# *Herbal smoking products are not considered tobacco product*, therefore, could be sold online. But new amendments to the Tobacco Law in LV could include a new type of product - tobacco substitute product - product, whether or not containing nicotine, intended to be used in a similar way as tobacco products, herbal smoking products, smokeless tobacco products, electronic smoking devices and refill containers. It would not be allowed to sell such tobacco substitute products online, thus soon it might be forbidden to sell herbal products online.
# I have updated C
# The same answer as for EE – The *law does not require adding such a tick box,* also it cannot be considered as a reason for not verifying the customer’s age, therefore, is not of much value. The ID check must be done using qualified means of electronic identification (usually Smart-ID) irrespective of the presence of such a tick box. Also, a courier delivering the products must verify the age of the recipient by requesting a valid ID, Thus, adding such a tick box is not mandatory (also not effective) but could be done upon the retailers/platform's own initiative.
# The same answer as for EE - the seller and couriers are liable. However, since a platform is playing a part in the alcohol distribution process, it should provide reasonable technical means to allow sellers/couriers to do the verification. Thus, the platform cannot completely be left out, but the main responsibility is still on the seller and the courier. Clause 2.8 of T&C for Partners in all three Baltic states (quoted above) provides some protection to us.
# For LT in particular such box ticking plays no role as it has been communicated by LT authorities that _“checking a box where the consumers themselves confirm that they are over the age of 20 to be insufficient and such a way cannot be considered as a reason for not verifying the customer’s age at the time of delivery.”_
# Please see my answer to Q5. In LT (I) Eater has to confirm with a checkbox "I am over 20 y.o & I can verify my age upon receipt”, (ii) Courier has to confirm with a checkbox "Verify the client's age" upon the delivery ← since there is no Smart ID check, we are not fully compliant. Will discuss it with my LT team. 
# Since platform engages in food handling activity, the platform could also be held liable to a certain extent if a platform operator does not exercise basis due diligence to preclude online selling of products that are forbidden. The main responsibility is still on the seller.
# LV – Yes, a separate “category” for alcohol is needed. However, there is no further regulation as how to do it – platform/ retailer is free to choose whether to add a new product category within the menu or create a new product page, etc. LT – my understanding is that alco must be separated also in LT. 
# Yes, correct.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

The Military Intelligence and Security Service has come back to us with a new request for us to provide the information that was previously asked. 

The police has stated - 

“We draw your attention to the fact that the status, competence, rights and obligations of the state security institutions, including the right to request and receive information, are confirmed in special regulatory acts, which stipulate that the activities of the state security institutions (National Security Law, State Security Institutions Law, Operative Act, etc.).

Article 19 of the Law on State Security Institutions, among other things, provides for the rights of officials of the state security institution to request and receive information, documents and other materials from state and local government institutions, merchants, organisations, officials and other persons, regardless of the ban on their use, receive the necessary information, documents and other materials about the services provided to individuals, as well as to obtain, register, process, collect, analyse and store information necessary for the performance of the functions of the relevant state security institution.

It should be noted that in accordance with the fourth part of Article 19 of the Law on State Security Institutions, the mentioned information can only be used for intelligence, counter-intelligence (including performing a personal check for access to the state
secret), within the framework of operational and criminal procedural activities.

We point out that the Military Intelligence Security Service is one of the three state security institutions, which in accordance with the National Security Law and the State Security Institutions
perform intelligence, counter-intelligence work and operative work tasks for the implementation of the tasks set by law for the national security system.

The Military Intelligence Security Service confirms that the information provided by SIA "Bolt Services LV" will be used only for the performance of its basic functions.



At the same time, we explain that Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and the Council of April 27, 2016 on the protection of natural persons applied to the processing of personal data and the free movement of such data and which repeals Directive 95/46/EC (hereinafter - the regulation) Article 2 provides that this regulation, among other things, does not apply to the processing of personal data in the course of work that does not fall within the scope of the Union legal acts (including in relation to national security). Recital 16 of the regulation also states that this regulation does not apply to questions about the protection of fundamental rights and fundamental freedoms or the free circulation of personal data related to activities that do not fall within the scope of Union rights, for example, activities related to state security. This regulation does not apply to the processing of personal data carried out by member states, acting in connection with the Union's common security policy and security policy.
Accordingly, the requirements of the regulation regarding the state security institution, including the Military Intelligence Security Service, do not apply to the right to request and receive information for the performance of their functions and tasks.
in view of the above, we ask you to provide the information requested by MIDD of October 19, 2023, request No. 5262-NOS/4/2-37ip/2023, October 23, 2023.

As [~accountid:5d53a63ba1f3290c16e637d6] has kindly pointed out a decision has previously been made on how to deal with passengers who add multi stops but decide to get out the vehicle earlier, please see ticket here - https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-21821. 

Please see advice which was put on the previous ticket: 

“For your logic below, you can do this provided the Driver and the Passenger agree to any significant reductions in pricing on a trip in the App (we shouldn’t be doing this for them or taking the burden of a refund). This is because the Driver accepts a trip on the basis it will be an estimated X amount and the Passenger agrees to pay that estimated X amount and that is how the contract is formed. 

Our TnCs generally accommodate changes if the fare is higher from the original estimate (such as due to traffic conditions), but not lower, like what you’ve outlined below. This is unless there is a change in fare destination or the ride has been cancelled - however - this still requires an action on behalf of the passenger to actively change their destination in the App and for the Driver to accept this as a revision on the agreement. 

Simply because a passenger changes their mind to get out earlier, does not give them an automatic right to a refund and we shouldn’t be refunding passenger for this unless they change their end destination in the App.  An example to understand this would be like a passenger buying a train ticket from destination A to B, just because they decide to jump off at an earlier station doesn’t given them a right to a reduced ticket price - they knew what they were purchasing at the time and agreed to this. 

In short: Drivers still need to be paid the amount they were expecting and the passenger is obligated to pay it, Bolt’s App simply assists them to do this”

*The problem :*
If ignition is on, in a state where it shouldn’t be, we get the following notification:
*UNEXPECTED_ACTIVITY*: ignition on
Most often it is for a short period of time, with the cars engine being blocked, and the car not moving, not causing any issues.
(As noticed it can be due the fact that user finishes the trip while being inside the car)
However, there are times, when the car is being driven in “hidden” status,
and currently we don’t have any specific alerts to notify this.Right now only way to notice these cars is manually checking all the ignition on alerts (which most often are cases where car was not moving),
or by noticing it in the car moving in the map view(which is not really applicable).

*The solution:*
Having an alert that shows up if a car is moving in hidden, would allow us to be aware of all these cases,
lowering the possibility of unsanctioned use and ensuring the safety of our cars.

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price) - i have took all the rides for Sep and the rider discount is 114.8 ( Ride price - Client paid)

!image-20231103-115617.png|width=1572,height=483!

!image-20231103-120113.png|width=722,height=471!



This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

*About the Booking Fees:*

We have booking fees which are part of order price and paid by the rider. We also have [fee calculators|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/billing-rides/feeCalculators/344833?tab=invoicingStrategy] for booking fees to charge booking fee amounts from the driver

_Dear [XXX],_ 

_Bolt understand the seriousness of this request and we seek to assist law enforcement whenever we can. We understand the need to treat your investigation as confidential._ 

_We note that your request has not provided us with adequate context surrounding the request. Article 5 GDPR states that any data that is provided to a third party is adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary for the purposes for which the data is processed. To enable Bolt to assess that the data requested falls under our duty of data minimisation, we ask that you kindly provide us with any relevant, necessary and proportional information and high-level context that relates to your request._

* _A reasoning why the information is requested and how this information pertains to the investigation of the alleged crime._

Hi everyone,

Based on my last last 1.1 with [~accountid:5afe99c869aa3d30612279da], it is my understanding that:

* In CY, passengers are charged an additional fee for scheduled trips to prevent them from booking scheduled trips for short distances because that would affect the supply and commercial dynamics.
* This additional fee is charged by the taxi drivers. However, taxi fares are regulated, so the taxi drivers are not supposed to charge more than the regulated fares.
* An inspector has warned the Ops team that taxi fares are regulated and that no such extra fee can be charged. In theory, the inspector could prosecute the taxi drivers.
* The Ops team does not envisage deactivating scheduled trips or eliminating the extra fee.

Since the Ops team is interested in maintaining both the scheduled trip feature and the additional charge for scheduled trips, +*the solution I propose to prevent taxi drivers from violating the regulation is for Bolt to charge passengers  a platform fee for scheduled trips,*+  rather than taxi drivers charging directly this additional fee.

To implement this new fee, we would have to obtain approval from Tax and Commerce by submitting the attached approval form to them. If we obtain approval to go ahead, we would have to justify this fee in our terms and conditions as a fee to maintain our technology, so that we can continue to benefit from the commercial agent exemption under the PSD2 Directive.

For a better context, when it comes to ride-hailing services, Bolt is considered to mediate payments from end users (i.e. riders) to service providers (i.e. drivers). This mediation is regulated in Europe by the PSD2 Directive and generally requires a financial services license, unless the payment mediator is eligible for a license exemption.

Specifically, Bolt, to mediate payments without a financial services license, relies on the so-called +commercial agent exemption+ regulated by article 3(b) of the PSD2 Directive. 

For Bolt to be eligible for such exemption, the following requirements must be met:

# Bolt must be an agent of payee (e.g. driver);
# Bolt must be authorized via an agreement to conclude and/or negotiate underlying services agreement on behalf of payee (e.g. transportation agreement on behalf of the driver);
# Bolt must perform the action described in section 2 above only on behalf of the of payee (e.g. Driver) and not on behalf of payer (e.g. rider).

For the sake of clarity, any fees charged by Bolt to the Riders must meet the requirements set out in the table below.



| |Requirement|Fees|
|Ride-hailing|As agent of driver/fleet Bolt concludes/negotiates the agreement for sale of transportation services on behalf of the driver/fleet.

Bolt must not do the same on Rider’s behalf.|Bolt should avoid fees, which could indicate that Bolt also offers services to riders in connection with the conclusion/negotiation of the transportation service agreement.

A fee that fits the above description and that *Bolt should therefore avoid* is, among others, the *fee for Bolt to help the rider find a driver.*

Bolt may instead apply fees that are not related to the negotiation of the conditions of the transportation service agreement
 for the benefit of the rider.|



*Considering the above explanation, how can we structure the Bolt riders fees to continue to relay on the commercial agent exemption?*

As you can see in the sign off form below, my proposal is to justify the booking fee as _a fixed charge to riders, in addition to the the fares for the transportation service provided by drivers and independent of these fares - applied to scheduled trips, intended to cover the additional costs incurred by Bolt given that for those scheduled trips Bolt needs to use more technological resources to make the application work properly for those scheduled trips._

*Parcel recipient did not show up*

*Step 1:* Provide general instructions

* Advise the driver to wait for the recipient for at least 5 minutes and try to reach them via a phone number provided by the client 
** {color:#006644}*In Lithuania, ask the driver to try to contact both the recipient and client for at least 15 minutes*{color}
* If the recipient did not show up and could not be reached out via a phone call, proceed with step 2

*Step 2:* Follow up with the report

* Ask the driver to contact the client to arrange a place where the parcel may be left for the recipient
** In Croatia, ask the driver to contact the client at least 3 times within 10 minutes to arrange the above
** If there is no such an option, proceed with the following
* Ask the driver to bring the parcel back to the client and inform them about the matter
* In Armenia, Azerbaijan, Croatia {color:#006644}*and Lithuania*{color}, the driver should finish the order when the parcel is returned to the client. 
** {color:#006644}*In Lithuania, if the driver does not agree with the final price after finishing the trip, they should request a Price Review with a description of what happened in the comment section. Do not complete a PR until all details are known and 24 hours passed since the time of the trip. While completing a PR, calculate the price based on the km and time spent on the way back to the client, compare it with the price suggested by the driver, and submit or modify it accordingly.*{color}
** In Romania, the ride back will be compensated manually
* In Ukraine, advise the driver to finish the order and bring the parcel to the client or to one of the approved offices. This should be done within 24 hours after the order or during the next business day if the order was placed on a weekend. Ask them to inform the client where the parcel was returned to.

*Note:* 

* In Croatia, if both client and recipient do not answer the calls, advise the driver to keep the parcel for some time. CS should try to connect the driver and the client later, so they can agree upon the parcel return.
* {color:#006644}*In Lithuania, if both the client and the recipient do not answer the calls, ask the driver to finish the trip and request a PR with a description of what happened in the comment section. Advise the driver to keep the parcel safe and keep trying to contact the client for the next 24 hours. If the client replies, they should agree on where to deliver the package. If there is no reply from the client, advise the driver to bring the parcel to the nearest police station and inform us where the parcel was left.* {color}

----

*Price recalculation*

In Romania and Ukraine, the order price does not change if the trip route is changed. In Azerbaijan, Armenia, Croatia {color:#006644}*and Lithuania*{color}, the price may be recalculated in such a case.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

That is indicated on the commission invoice

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So report show other calculations, but the commission invoice shows after ours deductions.

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

And dates are correct on the weekly report, as it shows only weekly calculations

h1. *Research - Request for Feature: Adding an Internal Board to Our Careers Portal*

We have carefully reviewed and researched the proposed feature of adding an internal board to our careers portal. This feature would restrict job applications to our employees and require Single Sign-On (SSO) and authentication. After thorough analysis, we regret to inform you that this feature request has been rejected. Below are the findings and reasons for this decision.

h2. *Reasons for Rejection*

h3. *1. Complexity and Cost*

*Complexity:* Implementing SSO and authentication for an internal job board can be intricate, involving integration with our company's authentication system and ensuring data security.

*Cost:* Developing and maintaining SSO and authentication systems can be expensive, necessitating dedicated resources, infrastructure, and ongoing maintenance.

h3. *2. Existing Access to Greenhouse*

Internal users within our organization already have direct access to Greenhouse, enabling them to apply for job openings. Given this existing access, the value of introducing a dedicated internal job board has been questioned.

h2. *Business Value Assessment*

We also considered the potential business value of this feature. In assessing the need for a separate internal job board, we evaluated the following factors:

h3. *Recruitment Needs*

While we acknowledge the importance of internal hiring, it was determined that the demand for hiring internal candidates may not justify the developer time and cost associated with implementing a separate internal job board. The existing Greenhouse platform serves as a well-established and accessible platform for all candidates.

h3. *Cost-Benefit Analysis*

Considering the potential benefits of this feature, like faster internal hiring, and thinking about the costs and potential downsides, such as development and upkeep expenses, it's clear that investing in this feature might not make sense, especially since internal candidates can already apply through Greenhouse.

h3. *Candidate Experience*

We also considered whether the introduction of authentication and a separate internal board genuinely enhances the candidate experience beyond what can be achieved through the existing Greenhouse platform. The existing platform already provides a seamless application process.

h2. *Conclusion*

After careful consideration, it has been determined that implementing an internal job board with SSO and authentication may not provide substantial additional value beyond what is already achieved through our existing Greenhouse platform. The complexity, cost, and existing accessibility for internal candidates led to the decision to reject this feature request.

We appreciate your proposal and thank you for your contribution to our continuous improvement efforts. If you have any further suggestions or feature requests, please feel free to submit them, and we will give each one careful consideration.

When an LTR UI changes RTL, these items are not mirrored:

* Numbers, such as those on a clock and phone numbers
* Untranslated text (even if it’s part of a phrase)
* Icons *that don’t communicate direction*, such as a camera, chat etc.

Mirroring a user interface results in the following changes:

* Text fields icons are displayed on the opposite side of a field
* Navigation buttons are displayed in reverse order
* *Icons that communicate direction*, like arrows, are mirrored
* Text (if it is translated to an RTL language) is aligned to the right

Hi there!

Thanks for this ticket. There are two main aspects to thisl the ‘reclassification side’ and the ‘data side’ (plus a minor point on the request for the users' gender).

*Reclass:*

As Bolt doesn’t provide transportation services, except in the UK, and because we don’t employ drivers, we need to balance: (a) our desire to improve safety + our rep with (b) also not holding ourselves out to be 100% responsible for safety. Ideally, we’d be a little vaguer with the following draft messaging, with reference to the safe use of our platform. 

+_Current wording:_+

_“We never stop looking for ways to make Bolt an even safer and more convenient way for you to move around.”_

_“We never stop looking for ways to make Bolt an even safer and more convenient way for you to earn.”_

+_Suggested alternative for both:_+

_“We never stop looking for ways to improve the safe use of our platform.”_

^^^this gets the same message across and links Bolt back to the ‘provider of the platform’ (which is correct) rather than implying anything else.

The sort of wording we’d always ideally avoid is anything along the lines of: [to passengers] _“we take our responsibility for your safety very serious and train all our drivers to minimise safety incidents”_. This is because:

(1) there is a soft representation that Bolt is wholly responsible; and
(2) Bolt doesn’t employ drivers so it shouldn’t be providing them with any training - if anything, we should only provide drivers with guidance to help reduce safety issues. 

These points carry over to all of our safety messaging, so it’s worth considering generally too. For other similar guidance, have a look at our conference page [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONTENT/pages/4468998200/Reclassification+Risk+Copy+Guide].

*Data:*

For quick reference, the relevant sentence in our comms is the following:

_“The survey takes about 1 minute to complete, and your answers are completely anonymous. We plan to use the collected data to make better-informed decisions on future developments.”_

From what has been said in the ticket request it looks to me that the results will not actually be anonymously held by Bolt and therefore ‘keeping the results confidential’ might be a better phrase, but I will need to defer to our privacy team. [~accountid:712020:ab85c798-bb67-4907-a29f-1443ba0f7414] - can you please review this ticket and let the safety team know your requirements? You’ll see that we are recording data in respect of this.

*Gender:*

The topic of gender is a very sensitive one in some markets so any questions along these lines should generally allow people to identify as they wish; there is no need to comment in depth but, for example, it makes sense to avoid any binary options. We will leave how this works to you, I’m just flagging the point 👌 

Many thanks.

Note to myself:

First thing coming to my mind related to this topic is maybe a question whether this type of practice (i.e communicating publicly offers in a way like it would be available to all users, but in reality offering these offers only to 90% of users) may qualify as *unfair commercial practice* OR as *misleading advertising*, especially in a case where we don´t use the promo code functionality (which would mean that actually this 10% control group who usually wouldn´t get the discount now has the chance to get the same discount when entering the promo code). 

According to the EE law what is based on EU law a[ |https://www.riigiteataja.ee/akt/119032019061?leiaKehtiv#para16][*trading practice is misleading* |https://www.riigiteataja.ee/akt/119032019061?leiaKehtiv#para16]*if (§ 16)* +the trader or service provider gives you false information about the goods or services or provides the correct information in a way that is likely to mislead you because it is unclear,+ incomprehensible, or ambiguous; +does not provide you with important information that you would need to know when making a purchase decision+ (e.g., +information about the+ main features and +price of the goods or services,+ maintenance and spare parts related to the use of the goods).

According to the[ EE law|https://www.riigiteataja.ee/en/eli/521122020005/consolide] *advertising shouldn´t provide inaccurate information* (§ 3 lg 3 p 11). Thereat, *advertising is considered misleading* in particular if it provides misleading information concerning the following circumstances characterising goods, services, sale of goods or provision of services: price and conditions of payment of the price (§ 4 lg 2 p 3). 

Based on this [+source+|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN-ET/TXT/?from=ET&uri=CELEX%3A52021XC1229%2805%29] and this [+source+ |https://europa.eu/youreurope/citizens/consumers/unfair-treatment/unfair-commercial-practices/index_en.htm]I would say that the practice we would like to use may most probably qualify as bait advertising which is one form of unfair commercial practice and also very closely related to misleading advertising. However, I didn´t find any info which would shed the light why we have chosen the threshold of 5% for the control group. I think this threshold was chosen back in the day based on the number of Bolt Food platform users taking just some % of it which would be potentially less harmful for us as a platform considering the risks described above.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Hey!

This is the regulation in our agreement:

*10.1* Without affecting any other right or remedy available to it, either party may terminate the Agreement with immediate effect by giving written notice to the other party, if:

*10.1.1*  the other party commits a material breach of any term of this Agreement which breach is incapable of remedy or if such breach is remediable fails to remedy that breach within *a period of five (5) days after being notified in writing* to do so with a warning of the possibility that the Agreement may be terminated. For the sake of clarity, if the Premises cannot be used for the Intended Purpose for at least 5 consecutive days or at least 10 days within a period of 6 months due to any reason that is independent from Bolt, this qualifies as a material breach.

So, the first step is to send the landlord a letter detailing the issue and give them time to remedy the issue. If they don’t manage that, we can proceed with the termination.

The clause they are breaching:

4.1.Bolt is entitled to use the Premises and Service area for any action necessary for carrying out online sales of goods (*Intended Purpose*), including but not limited to storing all kind of different goods (inter alia alcohol, tobacco, unpackaged goods etc) on the Premises, installing industrial refrigerators on the Premises for cooling down the goods, providing couriers with access to the Premises for picking up orders of the goods, providing access to suppliers to transport the goods to the Premises, *using Service area for stopping and parking vehicles that are needed for unloading goods or picking up orders etc.* The Landlord acknowledges that the Premises are used as a pickup location for online orders and therefore operations of Bolt might cause increased traffic and noise (from couriers, suppliers, garbage disposal providers) and has no complaints regarding this. Bolt is not entitled to use the Premises for other activity without written consent by the Landlord. Bolt is obligated at its own expense to provide all necessary approvals and permits for the operation of Bolt in the Premises; Bolt informs the Landlord about the requested and received licenses, permits, approvals, registration, etc.

Hi all! 



Whereas we do have a third-party liability insurance to cover our trips in Poland, this does not extend to parked scooters. 



It is mentioned by Zusanna in the ticket, it does not look like our scooter has caused the damage. - This is exactly the reason why we should reject liability for this damage - first, we have no control over who uses our *parked* scooters or not (it could have been any random person who could have damaged the gate with our scooter); second it can be the claimant themselves who placed our scooter there and causing the damage (or the damage was on the gate from some other incident and the claimant is now using our scooters to get the damage covered). 

Insurance-wise there’s not much to do, as we cannot claim this from our insurance provider. However, I would suggest we collect any evidence we have in our possession to demonstrate that this damage was not caused by our scooter. Furthermore, we should reject any liability as long as the claimant does not have undeniable proof that the damage was caused by our scooter. 

I know in some countries (e.g. Italy) Bolt would be jointly and severally liable as the owner of the scooter, however, I don’t think that’s the case in Poland. 



Best

Karmel

Hi [~accountid:61bc8e91150ace0069119e08] 

Unless they can prove without doubt our scooter/user caused this damage then not a lot we can do. 

All users/riders in Poland are provided with General Liability Insurance. Therefore, if they can confirm which rider caused this damages then we can pass this on to the insurance company to settle. 

However, if they are unable to provide evidence that we or our user caused this damage then our insurance provider will refuse to pay. 

We often get claims from similar businesses or car owners who claim our scooters fell over and damaged their property. 

However, without evidence to support their claim, there is not a lot we can do. 

I believe the legal team have templated letters for this type of interaction which say something like; 

“Thank you for contacting us and we are sorry your property has been damaged. However, since there is no evidence to prove that we and/or our users caused this damage, we are not in a position to compensate you etc…..”

Hi there, 

There was a user account opened for the particular number on 2022-07-31 and since then multiple devices to the account such as the ones you are seeing for the name Luccy. Bolt only checks the phone number itself by sending a confirmation code (OTP through SMS) during signup and sign-in. If the phone number holder signed to their account on different devices while having access to the number, then they can use those devices without having access to the number directly, until the account is deleted/archived or until a signout is prompted manually. 

How we see it is that the business allocated a number (work number) to the employee who then has the responsibility to treat that number according to their contract with the business. The question of whether the ex-employee had the authority to open an account for multiple devices with the work number should remain to be handled by the business internally. 

The main question we should raise here is whether were we notified of the employee, who had exclusive use of the phone number, being offboarded or not. As the business did not disable the phone number the access to the rider app was also not severed. Hence, it truly still comes down to the business admin informing us of a situation where they wish to keep using a number that previously was exclusively being used by another person. 

Based on the information so far, it looks like the business did not inform us and therefore they should pursue any actions with the ex-employee directly and/or with the help of authorities for opening & using this company’s resources in an unauthorised way. 

As a solution with the account, we can go ahead to delete it and then they can reopen a new clean one for the same number for which logins have to be confirmed again. We could also log out the previous devices from that account, however, the employee details will remain associated with the account until these are changed in the app by the owner of the number. 

Please let me know how you decide to proceed. If you can confirm the specific timelines and devices that the company itself owns then we can also help with the trips and account-related actions.

from pii.support_case_comments_v2 						as a
left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case 	as b
	on a.support_case_id = b.id 
left join admin_system.admin_system_city 				as c
	on b.city_id = c.id 
where 1=1
	and a.user_type in ('driver', 'rider', 'email', 'fleet_owner_company')
	and a.is_public = true 
	and a.case_language in ('en', 'gb')
	and date(a.created) >= date('2023-10-01')
	and date(a.created) <= date('2023-10-31') 
),
base_curated as (

	, array_intersect(comment_array, safety_keywords) 	as match_safety_keywords
from base
where 1=1
	and user_persona in ('rider', 'driver', 'driver_lead', 'fleet_owner', 'authority')
	and country_code = 'gb' 
)
select 
	created
	, support_case_id 
	, event_id 
	, case_language
	, country_code 
	, user_persona
	, cardinality(match_safety_keywords) 				as count_safety_words_in_comment
	, match_safety_keywords
from base_curated 
where 1=1
	and cardinality(match_safety_keywords)>0{code}

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So the numbers in the report and the commission invoice will never match.

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

A short discussion arose in Slack whether it’s appropriate to return an error in these cases.

In my opinion, the only scenario when the ip_info API is queried about these ranges, is when the request client IP is incorrectly passed along. If the request client IP is correctly passed along (from loadbalancer to service, down the chain of services, to the ip_info API), then there is no likelihood that these IP ranges will be requested.

ISPs and AWS itself will also restrict packets that originate in these source ranges on the network gateway level, most likely. We can confirm with neteng to make sure this is correct.

The positive value of highlighting an ip info request from an invalid range as an error, is related to quickly figuring out an error in the configuration of downstream services (who are passing the wrong IP)

The analysis was done on orders from a day in Bucharest, ~65k entries, comparing the 28.10 (Saturday) to the 30.10 (Monday) and the 02.11 (Thursday).

On Saturday, *66.61%* of orders had GPS location turned on (with no constraints on accuracy) and *47.7%* had a previous location in radius

!image-20231108-081627.png|width=695,height=545!

while during a weekday (Monday & Thursday, with a 07,% difference between them) an *extra 10% have location in radius* even though the percentage of cases where GPS is available stayed roughly the same.

!image-20231108-081824.png|width=695,height=545!


Out of the 66-67% entries with GPS, *89.2%* have a good {{gps_accuracy_m}} (<50) - the condition for auto-fit / auto-switch to trigger.

!image-20231108-082319.png|width=842,height=582!


On Saturday, auto-fit would be triggered ~3x as often as auto-switch

!image-20231108-082430.png|width=687,height=545!

While during a weekday, there’s a ~13% increase in auto-fit cases

!image-20231108-082508.png|width=687,height=545!

It would alter the behaviour for ~*13%* of cases on Thursday (*14.3%* for Monday) - auto-fit to a different location from the previous location.
Out of those 13%, *56% would match the order’s final delivery address* - in 56%, changing the location would be what the user wanted.
However, this estimate is rather pessimistic because the comparison is done on the auto-fitted address and final delivery location address and sometimes the same address is written in different ways (e.g. one has _Strada_ and the other _Str._), so the real number is higher. 
Distance distribution for the 44% that wouldn’t match (we’d change the address to something the user didn’t want). The second graph is a continuation of the first graph (the second graph doesn’t start at 0, it starts at 500, so 0-2000 is actually 500-2000).

If the pre-authorisation is successful, the guide states that the pre-authorised amount can differ from the final charge:

”I*f the pre-authorisation is successful* and after the ride is over, pre-authorisation amount can be captured or released:

It is captured when the +final price of the ride is equal to or smaller than the pre-authorisation+ (if it’s smaller, the rest of the amount is released)
When the +final price is higher than the pre-authorisation amount+, releasing or capturing the amount depends on fraud rules that require keeping the pre-authorised amount:
If there are none, the pre-authorisation is immediately released and the sum of the final price is authorised and charged
If there are any, the pre-authorisation is captured and the difference is added as a Bolt Balance debt”

Since we have the prior statement, and the guide tells how to identify a pre-authorisation within admin (the guide does not say that we need to look for an amount but to look for the _prepare_ or _authorisation_ label), I feel that the instructions are clear. Out all the entries where an _auto-fit location was present (_disregarding wether the same as previous or not), for *~91.5%** cases the *auto-fit address would match the final delivery address*, compared to *~87.8%** cases where the *previous location matches the final delivery address.* (this is for a weekday; for Saturday there’s a ~2% improvement of both these results).
*with the mention that the comparison is imperfect for both cases, so the real percentages of cases that match would be a little higher.
So in 3.7% of orders we save the user from having to switch the address themselves, potentially saving a portion of this ordering to the wrong address.

Situations when there are no locations in radius (auto-fit doesn’t trigger) but the GPS accuracy is good (<50m) - fallback strategy:
Keeping the *previous location as fallback* fails in *31.25% cases* (the final delivery address is different from the previous location address) with only *6.2%* within 50m.
Using *auto-switch* *as fallback* for those cases seems to fail in *78.58%* of times (the final delivery address is different from the reverse geocode address) with _21.7%_ of those failures being within _50m_ margin - some of which are faulty comparison but also cases where the address is across the street for example.

{noformat}WITH task_assigned AS (
    SELECT
        *
    FROM
        ng_beehive.beehive_task_task_event
    WHERE
        event_type = 'task_assigned' AND
        created >= date '2023-11-01'
)
SELECT
    DATE_DIFF('second', task_assigned.created, task_unassigned.created) AS diff,
    CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_unassigned.event_data, '$.version') AS INTEGER) - CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_assigned.event_data, '$.version') AS INTEGER) AS version_diff,
    JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_unassigned.event_data, '$.assignee.user_id') AS agent_id,
    task_assigned.created AS assigned_at,
    task_unassigned.created AS unassigned_at,
    task_assigned.task_id AS task_id,
    task_id.external_id AS external_id
FROM
    ng_beehive.beehive_task_task_event AS task_unassigned
JOIN
    task_assigned
ON
    task_assigned.task_id = task_unassigned.task_id AND
    JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_assigned.event_data, '$.assignee.user_id') = JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_unassigned.event_data, '$.assignee.user_id') AND
    CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_assigned.event_data, '$.version') AS INTEGER) < CAST(JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_unassigned.event_data, '$.version') AS INTEGER)
JOIN
    ng_beehive.beehive_task_task_id AS task_id
ON
    task_unassigned.task_id = task_id.id
WHERE
    task_unassigned.event_type = 'task_unassigned' AND
    JSON_EXTRACT_SCALAR(task_unassigned.event_data, '$.reason') = 'agent_offline' AND
    DATE_DIFF('second', task_assigned.created, task_unassigned.created) <= 60
ORDER BY
    assigned_at;{noformat}

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

[https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/71d0db7104fceb00032491b37e15bda15d17aba2/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/BillingDocumentService.ts#L497|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/71d0db7104fceb00032491b37e15bda15d17aba2/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/BillingDocumentService.ts#L497]

This function actually tries to parse as JSON of type {{AddressWithComponents}} - and only if failing, falling back to “string” address.

This {{recipient}} is of type {{Recipient | BusinessRecipientData}} . It can be {{user}} from order (for non business orders), or business agent, coming from either of those lines:

[https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4a79f14c6dfc5289b7b1e312474a03c6e02880b0/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/RecipientFacade.ts#L42|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4a79f14c6dfc5289b7b1e312474a03c6e02880b0/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/RecipientFacade.ts#L42] - Order User Data object

[https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4a79f14c6dfc5289b7b1e312474a03c6e02880b0/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/RecipientFacade.ts#L50|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4a79f14c6dfc5289b7b1e312474a03c6e02880b0/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/RecipientFacade.ts#L50] - unpacking a Work Profile object downloaded in line 32

or

[https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4a79f14c6dfc5289b7b1e312474a03c6e02880b0/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/RecipientFacade.ts#L80|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/4a79f14c6dfc5289b7b1e312474a03c6e02880b0/src/rental/marketplace/rental_billing/main/service/RecipientFacade.ts#L80] - Business Data object

So in theory, if the address coming from this facade is a JSON compatible with {{AddressWithComponents}}, then the invoice will have this address. But we haven’t tested.

From a regulatory standpoint, we have a handful of specific requirements concerning lost property in London and RoUK. We are obligated to *establish an “effective” lost property process*, maintain detailed records of lost property items for specified retention periods, and, when we come into possession of any lost property, return it

In London, we also need to demonstrate that *where practical, an attempt was made to return the item to the passenger*, and we need to provide evidence of this. This requirement is not overly prescriptive and can be achieved through other means than blocks

Given these regulatory requirements, my main concern revolves around the efficacy of our process if we were to remove the use of blocks. If passengers begin to complain excessively to TfL, we need to be able to defend our approach. *Reply to Skagstind*

* In the fist paragraph, I have suggested to replace _“. A couple of items”_ with _“,_ with _“[…] the following reservations concerning items that still need” [to be addressed]._ This is to ensure that we don’t accidentally waive any additional rights to compensation that we may have in relation to Skagstind under the agreement. 
* Question regarding Skagstind’s rights to remove our branding in connection with private events: The contract including Attachment A does not say anything about that, i.e. Skagstind does not have such a right (unless it has been agreed separately somehow, which I am not aware of).
* Question regarding exclusivity in connection with the campaign, particularly relating to Instagram posts involving Foodora: 
** There is an exclusivity clause (6) in the agreement, but it only applies to 'competitors of Bolt operating in the taxi industry in Oslo', and the exclusivity refers only to the marketing channels specified in the agreement, i.e. the venues listed in clause 4 of the agreement and Attachment A, excluding Instagram.
** There are no obstacles from a legal perspective preventing you from raising this even though Skagstind is not contractually prohibited to promote Foodora. However, it may lead to a discussion which may in turn affect negotiations. I recommend considering the benefits of leaving it in, e.g. if it may increase the value of the campaign/agreement for Bolt going forward, and whether the possible benefits outweigh the risk of ‘bugging’ Skagstind by bringing up something new at this point in the negotiations. An alternative would be just expressing our concerns and asking what they can do about it, they may be willing to take it down now that they have admitted their wrongs 🙂 
* I have suggested to delete or amend the last paragraph (_“I will continue the conversation with NoHo Partners regarding the way forward for Raadhuset, Vulkan …”)_. 
** In this instance, it should be noted that regardless of whether NoHo decides to continue the campaigns in their venues, even if it's free of charge, this does not relieve Skagstind from their contractual undertakings, unless we say so. 
** *Unless we have explicit confirmation from NoHo’s of to which extent and how they will take over Skagstind’s responsibility in writing yet, I don’t think we should mention them in the email to Skagstind for now.* 
** Clause 13 of the agreement allows for assignment of rights and obligations to a third party provided that the respective parties give their prior written consent. To do this, we can explicitly provide our consent for Skagstind to assign its rights and obligations under the agreement with respect to the sold venues to NoHo, with the reservation of obtaining written confirmation from both Skagstind and NoHo.The assignment would basically mean that NoHo takes Skagstind's place in the agreement with Bolt, only in relation to the sold venues. Also, as an FYI, a proper assignment may entitle NoHo to claim the part of the contract sum pertaining to the sold venues from Skagstind.
** An alternative would be continuing to hold Skagstind liable for the breach of contract with respect to the sold venues. However, in order for us to have any right to compensation for this from a legal perspective, we would have to prove what loss we have suffered due to the breach. Since NoHo has agreed to take over Skagstind’s responsibility for the execution of the campaign in these venues, it could be argued that we would have a hard time proving this. 

*General considerations regarding the settlement amount: Total lost estimated visitors per week*

Whether to settle and for how much is ultimately up to business in this case. However, I still want to make sure that all factors have been taken into consideration before accepting the settlement offer of NOK 100,000 from Skagstind. Considering the vast extent of Skagstind’s contract breach, it could be higher, especially if NoHo for some reason backs off from executing the campaign in Skagstind’s place with respect to the sold venues. Please see further details below.

In total, (1) the closing of Pokalen Aker Brygge; (2) the possible exclusion of Restaurant Bestorp; (3) the sale of the venues listed above, and (4) the Telegrafen incident, entail a loss of 9194 estimated visitors per week, which is equivalent to 85% of the 10826 estimated visitors per week in total when the agreement was signed (see Attachment A).

If the above would serve as basis for deciding on a refund amount that would reflect the extent of Skagstind’s contract breach, Bolt would be entitled to *repayment of 85% of the contract sum, which is NOK 212500*.

In addition, a compensation of 85% would not cover for other losses, e.g. pertaining to Skagstind’s failure to use the agreed assets in the respective venues (see +Attachment A+). For example, Casa Pisano has not allowed stickers, although assets in Casa Pisano include posters, flyers, _QR code stickers_, coasters according to +Attachment A+. Also, it should be noted that Casa Pisano was one of the original venues in the agreement, i.e. Casa Pisano was never a substitute for Restaurant Bestorp as Skagstind tried to argue when they suddenly closed it. These types of incidents have probably also resulted in a decrease in the number of people who have seen the campaign, compared to what Bolt could have reasonably expected when signing the agreement/paying the contract sum.

I hope this is helpful.

Please let me know if you have any questions or wish to discuss. 

Best regards,

Ida

{noformat}acq_disc_q = """

select date_trunc('day',created_date) as date_day, city, 
sum( case when app_version like '%CA%' then gmv else 0 end) as gmv_android, 
sum(case when app_version like '%CA%' then total_bonus else 0 end) as total_bonus_android,
sum( case when app_version like '%CI%' then gmv else 0 end) as gmv_ios, 
sum(case when app_version like '%CI%' then total_bonus else 0 end) as total_bonus_ios
from ng_public_spark.etl_incentives_order_metrics eiom
inner join ng_public_spark.etl_first_finished_ride_for_user fr
on eiom.order_id = fr.order_id and eiom.city_id = fr.city_id
where city in ('Johannesburg', 'Paris', 'Berlin', 'Lisbon', 'Madrid', 'Tallinn', 'Bucharest', 'Prague', 'Warsaw', 'Accra', 'Nairobi', 'Lagos') 
and created_date <= date('2023-09-01')
group by 1,2
order by 1 desc
"""

The calculation of the average cost is based on put-aways which can be reported on dates much later than shipment dates (on which the accounting is based). This results in different amounts in the company's currency (if stock request is in another currency then company currency). 
For example, KS-5-13 - 3A Charger:

21.08  100 * 8.44EUR = 844 EUR.    844*1.8500 = 1561.40 AZN

23.08  100 * 8.44EUR = 844 EUR.    844*1.8544 = 1561.11 AZN
Total *accounting* balance = *4691.62 AZN*.
Total accounting balance in EUR 08.11.2023 = 4691.62/1.82011 = 2577.66 EUR

And 3 put-away
04.10  100 * 8.44EUR = 844 EUR.    844*1.779 = 1501.47 AZN
31.10  100 * 8.44EUR = 844 EUR.    844*1.7952 = 1515.15 AZN

Total amount = *4531,77 AZN* (I*nventory Site Balance*). Average cost = 4531.77/300 = 15.105912 AZN
Total Inventory Site Balance in EUR 08.11.2023 = 4531.77/1.8201 = 2489.85 EUR

Command to retrieve data for history:

{noformat}$ elastic-cli -c "query.additional_parameters" -q 'node.path: "/internal/v2/pciSupport/findCardInstrumentId" AND node.package_name: "live-paymentinstrument" AND node.log_message: "Find card instrument id V2 request"' -o "user_id|card_" -e -f "2023-11-07T19:00:00.000Z" -t "2023-11-08T19:00:00.000Z" -R --recurrent-index 'logs-envoy-external*access*' --recurrent-query 'http.path: "/client-commerce-proxy/user/v2/pciSupport/findCardInstrumentId" AND query.version: "CA.2.90" AND query.device_name: "samsungSM-G935F"' --recurrent-batch-size 1000 | jq -cr '(.user_id|tostring) + " " + (.card_bin|tostring) + " " + (.card_last4|tostring) + " " + .card_expiry' > output_file{noformat}

Takes roughly ~1 min
How it works:

# Find all root_hash-es from query {{http.path: "/client-commerce-proxy/user/v2/pciSupport/findCardInstrumentId" AND query.version: "CA.2.90" AND query.device_name: "samsungSM-G935F"}}  (~163k hashes)
# Then search for {{node.path: "/internal/v2/pciSupport/findCardInstrumentId" AND node.package_name: "live-paymentinstrument" AND node.log_message: "Find card instrument id V2 request AND root_hash: (... found hashes ...)"}} and takes {{user_id}} and {{card_*}}  from it (~160 requests to Elastic Search, generates ~150k matched rows)
