We have now received the advice note from external counsel to determine if Bolt is in breach of the following Licence Agreements: 

# *_Sefton_*
# *_Blackburn_*
# *_Brighton_*

We asked external counsel to determine the following: 

_If Bolt is in breach of the Licence Agreements as a result of:_ 

# the actual use of those premises, which are ‘cloud based private hire operations’ versus what is permitted under the Licence Agreements’ terms; or
# previous change of use planning applications which were made without the landlord’s/licensor’s (prior) consent.

*AND* 

#   _For any potential breach identified above:_
##  the implications of such a breach; and
##  what practical steps Bolt can take to mitigate the risks or remedy the breach(es).

 Please see comments for each Licence Agreement below: 

{color:#0747a6}+*1.THE SEFTON LICENCE*+{color}

 {color:#0747a6}*Permitted vs Actual.*{color}

*  The Sefton Licence allows Bolt to use Office 5 for "General Office Use," although this term is not precisely defined and open to interpretation. On a strict interpretation, "cloud-based private hire operations" might be seen as a breach of this use, but a broader interpretation takes into account the parties' likely intentions and the overall circumstances. In this broader context, it could be argued that Bolt’s use for "cloud-based private hire operations" is consistent with what a reasonable person might consider within the scope of "general office use." For example, there may be a set number of staff working at Office 5, work may be limited to the Permitted Hours and customers/ general members of the public may not attend Office 5.

{color:#0747a6}*Summary* {color}

Given the wide scope for interpretation of the permitted use, external counsel cannot provide us with a definitive view as to whether the actual use breaches the permitted use clause. It is arguable either way.

 {color:#0747a6}*Planning Application*{color}

*  The Sefton Licence does not contain any restrictions on making planning applications and did not require Bolt to seek the Licensor’s consent. As such there is no breach of the Sefton Licence here in respect of any past planning applications.
* As an aside, having looked on the local planning authority’s portal, it appears that Bolt made an application to change the authorised use to B1 (a) - Office (Other than A2) (Reference No: DC/2021/02627) but later withdrew that application. The attached Approval Notice (Reference No: DC/2019/02224) dated 25th February 2020 authorised Office 5 for use as a taxi hire office (sui generis). Unless there is a later permission for “cloud based private hire operations” then the taxi hire office use will continue for planning legislation purposes. I only flag this in case that it is significant for Bolt outside the scope of this advice note.

{color:#0747a6} *Implications and practical advice*{color}

*  Under clause 5, the Licensor has the right to terminate the agreement without notice if Bolt fails to perform and observe the terms and conditions of the agreement. 
* If the Landlord took the technical interpretation of the user clause then it could argue there has been a breach of the user clause and would have the right to terminate the Sefton Licence without notice. A termination of the agreement would not affect any prior rights or remedies available to the Licensor against Bolt. The Landlord would need to establish a contractual claim and prove it had suffered an actual loss stemming from the breach of user clause in order to recover any monetary damages from Bolt.
*  But practically, if the actual use causes no nuisance to other occupiers within the Building and does not prejudice the insurance cover, then the risk of the Landlord taking a strict/technical interpretation and alleging a breach of the Licence terms is considered to be remote but not impossible.
*  Please note, the Sefton Agreement is purportedly terminable by either party giving just one months’ notice to the other. This is on a “no fault” basis and does not require any breach of the Sefton Licence’s terms for the Licensor to trigger this termination right.
*  I say “purportedly” because Bolt’s interest in the Sefton Agreement is assignable with the Licensor’s prior consent which is very unusual for a licence to occupy. These are usually personal interests only and incapable of assignment. That may open the door for an argument that the “licence” is actually a tenancy but that is outside the scope of my instructions in the Work Required. I have not considered this technical point in any detail. 

{color:#0747a6} *Options available to Bolt*{color}

#  Bolt could consider seeking the Licensor’s confirmation that your actual use of Office 5 is not inconsistent with the Permitted Use. That may have negative consequences if the Landlord disagrees and could actually prompt the Landlord to terminate the Sefton Licence.
# If continued occupation at Office 5 is crucial to Bolt then the recommendation would be to  engage with the Licensor to discuss the possibility of putting in place an alternative arrangement with a long term and more security for Bolt. However, flexibility may suit both Bolt and the Licensor. 
# If the Licensor agrees to do so, Bolt should seek to vary the Permitted Use in the new agreement to make it clear that Bolt can use Office 5 for its actual use.

 

{color:#ff991f}*2. THE BLACKBURN LICENCE*{color}

 {color:#ff991f}*Permitted vs Actual.*{color}

* The Blackburn Licence replaced the Former Blackburn Agreement which was a mere tenancy at will and determinable on notice. The Former Blackburn Agreement can now be disregarded. 
* The Blackburn Licence grants Bolt the right to occupy Unit 13 for “office use for Bolt Services UK”). The same comments on strict interpretation made in respect of the Sefton Licence apply to the Blackburn Licence. On a broad interpretation, “cloud based private hire operations” may be consistent with “office use for Bolt Services UK” but that is a matter of fact having regard to all the circumstances, the likely intention of the parties and characteristics of Bolt’s actual use of Unit 13.
* It is not possible to give a definitive answer as to whether Bolt’s actual use of Unit 13 breaches the Blackburn Licence.

{color:#ff991f} *Planning Application*{color}

* In contrast to the Former Blackburn Agreement, the Blackburn Licence does not contain any restrictions on making planning applications and did not require Bolt to seek the Council’s prior consent.
*  In fact, the Blackburn Licence made Bolt “responsible for …. obtaining and complying with any planning permission” (para 13). As such the past planning application would be consistent with complying with that obligation and would not be a breach of the Blackburn Licence.
*  A Decision Notice was sourced (10/22/0597 dated 17 August 2022) from the local planning authority’s portal. This authorised the change of use for Unit 13 to taxi booking office (sui generis) not “cloud based private hire operations”.  

{color:#ff991f}*Implications and practical advice*{color}

* The Blackburn Licence does not grant the Council any right to terminate the Blackburn Licence in response to a breach of the Licence terms nor does it set out any remedies for any purported breach.
*  As with the Sefton Licence, the Council would need to prove breach of contractual term and prove it had suffered an actual loss stemming from the breach of user clause if it were to seek to recover any monetary damages from Bolt.
*  Practically, enforcement action by the Council seems unlikely as either party can terminate the Blackburn Licence on 4 weeks’ written notice (para 8). This right exists on “a no fault” basis.
*  The Licence period also expires on 11 December 2023 (para 3) so the risk of any enforcement action by the Council is diminishing by the day.

{color:#ff991f}*Options available to Bolt*{color}

Given the upcoming Licence expiry date, if continued occupation at Unit 13 is important to Bolt then Bolt should approach the Council with a request to renew the Licence. You may wish to discuss the possibility of putting in place an alternative arrangement with a longer term and more security for Bolt. But flexibility may suit both parties.

Any new arrangement with the Council should make clear that Bolt can use Unit 13 for its actual use for the avoidance of any doubt / mitigating the risk of any enforcement action.



{color:#36b37e}*3. THE BRIGHTON LICENCE*{color}

{color:#36b37e} *Permitted vs Actual.*{color}

The Brighton Licence authorises Bolt to occupy Unit E5a for the Permitted Use which is defined in the particulars of the Agreement as “Information and Communication”.  There is a restriction in clause 10 on using Unit E5a for any purposes other than the Permitted Use. 

 The term “Information and Communication” is not defined in the Agreement, and so, what is and what is not permitted is unclear. There is scope for interpretation on a similar basis as outlined above for the other Licence Agreements.

 On a technical interpretation Bolt may well be in breach of the user clause of the Brighton Licence. Whether “cloud based private hire operations” is a use consistent with “Information and Communication” is unclear. There is a risk that BizSpace may disagree with the actual use and take enforcement action for breach of the user clause but see my comments below on the likelihood of this.

There may be scope to argue against such an argument under contra proferentem rule. This rule can apply in certain circumstances where there is ambiguity in an agreement. If the rule applies the ambiguity would be construed against BizSpace. For the rule to apply the Licence terms would need to have been “imposed” by BizSpace on Bolt, i.e. without any negotiation.

{color:#36b37e}*Planning Application*{color}

* The Brighton Licence does not contain any restrictions on making planning applications and did not require Bolt to seek BizSpace’s prior consent.
* The Brighton Licence obliged Bolt to “comply with all relevant laws and regulations” and this would include compliance with planning legislation. If a change of use application was required from Bolt to comply with its actual use of Unit E5a then that application was made pursuant to the terms of the Brighton Licence and not in breach. But compliance with planning legislation would not cure a breach of the contractual user clause.
* I was unable to find any planning decisions on the local planning authority’s portal. I attach a screenshot showing the property address with no planning history showing. @Elise Do you have a copy of the planning application in case this has been misfiled by the LPA?

{color:#36b37e} *Implications and practical advice*{color}

# The Brighton Licence contains a right for BizSpace to immediately terminate the arrangement if Bolt breaches any of the terms of the agreement and fails to rectify that breach immediately after receipt of notice from BizSpace (clause 17).
#  There is an indemnity provision in clause 18 obliging Bolt to indemnify BizSpace against “any losses, damages, costs, expenses, liability and claims whether resulting directly or indirectly from Your occupation and use of the Unit(s) …. or any breach of this Agreement”. Unlike the other Licence Agreements, as a result of the indemnity provisions, Bolt has already promised to meet such liabilities and BizSpace would not need to establish a contractual right to recover. Bolt would be liable for any such liabilities whether directly or indirectly stemming from its occupation of Unit E5a or breach of the Brighton Licence’s terms.
# Either party can terminate the Brighton Licence on 4 weeks’ written notice (clause 19). This termination right is on “a no fault” basis. Termination would be without prejudice to any antecedent rights or remedies of BizSpace against Bolt.
#  Practically, if the actual use causes no nuisance to other occupiers within the Centre, does not prejudice the insurance cover in place, and is not detrimental to BizSpace then the risk of BizSpace taking a strict/technical interpretation and alleging a breach of the Licence terms may well be remote. But that eventuality cannot be entirely ruled out.

{color:#36b37e}*Action points:*{color}

# Bolt could consider seeking BizSpace’s confirmation that the actual use of Unit E5a is not inconsistent with the Permitted Use. But that may have negative consequences if BizSpace disagrees and may actually prompt termination of the Brighton Licence in a worst-case scenario.
# If continued occupation at Unit E5a is important to Bolt then I would recommend you engage with BizSpace to explore the possibility of putting in place an alternative arrangement with more security, i.e. removing the rolling termination right. 
# If BizSpace agrees to do so, Bolt should also seek to vary the Permitted Use in the new agreement to make it clear that Bolt can use Unit E5a for its actual use.

{color:#bf2600}+*SUMMARY OF THE SEFTON, BLACKBURN & BRIGHTON LICENCE AGREEMENTS*+ {color}

# It is difficult to give a firm view on whether Bolt’s actual uses of these premises breaches the terms of the Licence Agreements given the vague wording of their permitted uses. It is arguable either way on a strict vs broad interpretation approach. But if the actual use is not causing any harm then enforcement action may well be remote, not least, because the Licence Agreements are all determinable on a “no fault” basis and on short notice. If the premises are crucial to Bolt then it may wish to engage with the Licensors under each of the Licence Agreements to explore alternative terms. Any such new agreements should look to address the vague wording of the permitted use.
# The Licence Agreements do not prohibit planning applications without the Licensors’ prior consent so there is no arguable breach here for past planning applications. Whether the current uses authorised by planning legislation align with Bolt’s actual use of these premises and/or “cloud based private hire operations” is a separate point outside the scope of the Work Required and this advice note.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

4) To fix step 3, I have to divide 1122 = 1120+2, and 10% VAT is added only to 1120. Giving the total amount as 1234 and everything is correct. 

So, all in all, I believe everything comes down to digits after comma.

query (presto) to case_comments

{code:sql}with base as (
select 
	a.created
	, a.support_case_id
	, a.event_id 
	, a.case_language 
	, split(regexp_replace(lower(a.comment),'\W', ' '), ' ') 		as comment_array 
	, a.user_type
	, b.city_id
	, b.user_persona
	, b.order_id 
	, c.country_code 
	, array ['unsafe','safety','endangered','forced','spat','physically','wheelchair','crutch','crutches','cash','risk','shag','prostitute','flirt','flirting','nigger','nigga','racially','paki','slur','gay','fag','faggot','faggots'] 								as safety_keywords
from pii.support_case_comments_v2 						as a
left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case 	as b
	on a.support_case_id = b.id 
left join admin_system.admin_system_city 				as c
	on b.city_id = c.id 
where 1=1
	and a.user_type in ('driver', 'rider', 'email')
	and a.is_public = true 
	and a.case_language in ('en', 'gb')
	and date(a.created) >= date('2023-10-01')
	and date(a.created) < date('2023-11-01') 
),
base_curated as (
select *
	, array_intersect(comment_array, safety_keywords) 	as match_safety_keywords
from base
where 1=1
	and user_persona in ('rider', 'driver')
	and country_code = 'gb' 
)
select 
	created
	, support_case_id 
	, order_id
	, city_id
	, event_id 
	, user_persona
	, match_safety_keywords
	, cardinality(match_safety_keywords) 				as count_safety_words_in_comment
from base_curated 
where 1=1
	and cardinality(match_safety_keywords)>0{code}

h3. User cannot reserve a vehicle/order a trip due to negative Bolt Balance

If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:

*Step 1: Confirm charge details*

* Open User Balance > [Transaction history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
* Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
* Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
* Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date

*Step 2: Verify the cause*

* Open the Fraud > Calculations > [User page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
* Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
* Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.


If you need any further information, let me know. 
Best Regards,

{code:sql}WITH configs AS (
    SELECT
        id,
        id = MIN(id) OVER(PARTITION BY city_id) AS is_min_id,
        city_id,
        max_multiplier
    FROM ng_public_spark.pricing_config_dynamic_pricing_configuration
    WHERE status = 'exposing'
),

max_multipliers AS (
    SELECT
        co.city_id,
        max_multiplier
    FROM configs co
    LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.admin_system_city AS ci ON ci.id = co.city_id
    WHERE is_min_id
),

_order AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(o.city_id AS INT) AS city_id,
        o.id AS order_id,
        o.user_id,
        o.created AS order_created,
        o.state AS order_state,
        o.lat AS pickup_lat,
        o.lng AS pickup_lng,
        o.destination_lat,
        o.destination_lng,
        prr.surge_multiplier_type AS multiplier_type,
        prr.surge_multiplier AS multiplier,
        prr.predicted_price AS price,
        prr.duration,
        prr.distance,
        mm.max_multiplier,
        popc.multiplier AS failed_order_multiplier,
        popc.is_confirmed AS is_failed_order_confirmed,
        popc.created AS failed_order_created,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY o.city_id, o.id ORDER BY s.created DESC) s_rn
    FROM core.search_categories_overview AS s
    INNER JOIN core.search_categories_overview_category AS sc ON (
        s.search_categories_overview_token = sc.search_categories_overview_token
        AND UNIX_TIMESTAMP(sc.created) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(s.created) = 0
        AND ABS(
            CAST(
                SUBSTR(
                    s.search_categories_overview_token,
                    3, INSTR(s.search_categories_overview_token, '_') - 3
                ) AS BIGINT
            )
            / 1000.0
            - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(s.created)
        ) < 1
    )
    INNER JOIN pricing.price_prediction_result_rate prr ON (
        s.price_prediction_token = prr.price_prediction_token
        AND sc.search_category_id = prr.search_category_id
    )
    INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS o ON (
        s.session_id = o.session_id
        AND s.city_id = o.city_id
        AND o.created_date BETWEEN DATE '{min_date}' AND DATE '{max_date}'
        AND s.created < o.created
    )
    INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_search_filter as sf ON (
        o.id = sf.id
        AND o.city_id = sf.city_id
    )
    INNER JOIN max_multipliers AS mm ON o.city_id = mm.city_id
    INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.pricing_order_price_confirmation AS popc ON (
        o.city_id = popc.city_id
        AND o.id = popc.order_id
    )
    WHERE TRUE
        AND s.created_hour BETWEEN DATE '{min_date}' AND DATE '{max_date}'
        AND sc.created_hour BETWEEN DATE '{min_date}' AND DATE '{max_date}'
        AND prr.created_hour BETWEEN DATE '{min_date}' AND DATE '{max_date}'
        AND popc.created_date BETWEEN DATE '{min_date}' AND DATE '{max_date}'
        AND o.city_id IN ({city_ids})
        AND popc.city_id IN ({city_ids})
        AND sf.filter_search_category_id = sc.search_category_id
        AND popc.multiplier IS NOT NULL
),

order AS (
    SELECT * EXCEPT(s_rn) FROM _order WHERE s_rn = 1
),

drivers_rejected AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(cot.city_id AS INT) AS city_id,
        cot.order_id,
        SORT_ARRAY(COLLECT_LIST(NAMED_STRUCT(
            'order_try_created', cot.created,
            'id', cot.driver_id,
            'lat', CAST(cot.driver_lat AS FLOAT),
            'lng', CAST(cot.driver_lng AS FLOAT),
            'eta', cot.time_to_client,
            'b2b', CAST(cot.search_algorithm = 'b2b' AS INT)
        )), TRUE) AS drivers_rejected
    FROM ng_public_spark.pricing_order_price_confirmation AS popc
    INNER JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try AS cot
        ON popc.city_id = cot.city_id AND popc.order_id = cot.order_id
    WHERE TRUE
        AND popc.created_date BETWEEN '{min_date}' AND '{max_date}'
        AND cot.created_date BETWEEN '{min_date}' AND '{max_date}'
        AND popc.city_id IN ({city_ids})
        AND cot.city_id IN ({city_ids})
        AND popc.multiplier IS NOT NULL
        AND cot.created < popc.created
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),

_drivers_available AS (
    SELECT
        mr.city_id,
        mro.order_id,
        mr.created AS matching_round_created,
        popc.created AS foo_created,
        srd.driver_id,
        srd.lat,
        srd.lng,
        srd.duration_till_pickup,
        srd.pos,
        CAST(srd.algorithm = 'b2b' AS INT) AS b2b,
        CASE
            WHEN mr.created IS NOT NULL THEN DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY mr.city_id, mro.order_id ORDER BY UNIX_TIMESTAMP(popc.created + INTERVAL 1 SECONDS) - UNIX_TIMESTAMP(mr.created), mr.created)
            ELSE NULL
        END AS rn
    FROM ng_public_spark.pricing_order_price_confirmation AS popc
    LEFT JOIN rides.matching_round_order AS mro
        ON popc.city_id = mro.city_id
            AND popc.order_id = mro.order_id
    LEFT JOIN rides.matching_round AS mr
        ON mr.city_id = mro.city_id
            AND mr.round_id = mro.round_id
    LEFT JOIN core.search_result AS sr
        ON mro.city_id = sr.city_id
            AND mro.order_id = sr.order_id
            AND CAST(mro.search_token AS BIGINT) = sr.search_token
    LEFT JOIN core.search_result_driver AS srd
        ON sr.id = srd.search_log_id
    WHERE TRUE
        AND mr.created_hour BETWEEN '{min_date}' AND '{max_date}'
        AND mro.created_hour BETWEEN '{min_date}' AND '{max_date}'
        AND sr.created_hour BETWEEN '{min_date}' AND '{max_date}'
        AND TO_DATE(CAST(srd.created_date AS STRING)) BETWEEN '{min_date}' AND '{max_date}'
        AND popc.created_date BETWEEN '{min_date}' AND '{max_date}'
        AND mr.city_id IN ({city_ids})
        AND mro.city_id IN ({city_ids})
        AND popc.city_id IN ({city_ids})
        AND (
            (mr.created BETWEEN popc.created - INTERVAL 1 SECONDS AND popc.created + INTERVAL 1 SECONDS)
            OR mr.created IS NULL
        )
        AND popc.multiplier IS NOT NULL
),

drivers_available AS (
    SELECT
        CAST(city_id AS INT) AS city_id,
        order_id,
        matching_round_created,
        SORT_ARRAY(COLLECT_LIST(NAMED_STRUCT(
            'position', pos,
            'id', driver_id,
            'lat', CAST(lat AS FLOAT),
            'lng', CAST(lng AS FLOAT),
            'eta', duration_till_pickup,
            'b2b', b2b
        )), TRUE) AS drivers_available
    FROM _drivers_available
    WHERE rn = 1 OR rn IS NULL
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
)

SELECT
    o.*,
    dr.drivers_rejected,
    CASE
        WHEN da.drivers_available IS NULL THEN ARRAY()
        ELSE da.drivers_available
    END AS drivers_available,
    TO_DATE(failed_order_created, 'yyyy-MM-dd') AS created_date
FROM order AS o
LEFT JOIN drivers_rejected AS dr ON (
    o.city_id = dr.city_id
    AND o.order_id = dr.order_id
)
LEFT JOIN drivers_available AS da ON (
    o.city_id = da.city_id
    AND o.order_id = da.order_id
){code}

Once we have modified the battery pack, the original manufacturer cannot be held liable for it, but we can.

Article 7, "Duty to cooperate".

* The public administrations, as well as any natural or legal person, shall provide the judicial authorities, the Public Prosecutor's Office or the Judicial Police with the data, reports, background information and supporting documents requested by them and which are necessary for the investigation and prosecution of criminal offences or for the execution of penalties. The request of the Judicial Police must be adjusted exclusively to the exercise of the functions entrusted to it by article 549.1 of Organic Law 6/1985, of 1 July and must always be made in a reasoned, concrete and specific manner, always informing the judicial and prosecutorial authorities.

The communication of data, reports, background information and supporting documents by the Tax Administration, the Social Security Administration and the Labour and Social Security Inspectorate shall be carried out in accordance with their respective legislation.

* In other cases, public administrations, as well as any natural or legal person, shall provide data, reports, background information and supporting documents to the competent authorities that request them, provided that these are necessary for the specific performance of their tasks for the prevention, detection and investigation of criminal offences and for the prevention and protection against a real and serious danger to public safety. 

The request of the competent authority must be concrete and specific and contain the reasons that accredit its relation to the aforementioned cases.

* The provisions of the previous subsections shall not be applicable when judicial authorisation is legally required to collect the data necessary for compliance with the purposes of Article 1.



* In the cases contemplated in the preceding paragraphs, the data subject shall not be informed of the transmission of his data to the competent authorities, nor of having provided access to them by those authorities in any other way, in order to ensure the security of the data.

I’ve just now been able to catch up on all comments. Let me shed some lights on the operation globally. 

# In terms of contract, scouts across all of Africa are asked to sign a [*main service agreement*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o00v8xQhoM4X_yhJW453sMkFaCi6i4KHtF8B6sCVT28/edit?usp=sharing] and a [*data processing agreement*|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1KknxXIhNXCuSw_nYCW90U50iAU9jqlJ4-dHaFk-NUXQ/edit?usp=sharing].  
# There are multiple ways to ensure scouts will receive their payments. 
## most popular method in Africa is to assign very old driver accounts from 2019/2020, which have never been used again and have 0 activity, 0 trip. This helps not affecting any performance numbers.
## in Ukraine and Tunisia, we’ve been creating ourselves new driver accounts using SCOUT as name. Doing so impacted the number of registrations but not activations. It was okay in those markets as the scale is not the same as african markets.
## In Azerbaijan, we chose a referral code that was not associated with a driver account, and payments were done through an agency on a monthly basis who was taking a fee and redistributing the money to the agents on our behalf.

In the case of a & b, going through Admin accounts mean we can automate payments and scouts have visibility through their account. It also creates an invoice in the same way as it would do for a driver so whoever pays the drivers will be paying scouts in this situation. However based on each market’s regulation we would adapt this methodology. 

Moreover a & b is not accepted for the long term, I am in discussion with our Product to find a longer term solution to have a dedicated process for scouts so we no longer touch any driver accounts.

long answer with more details on what we actually want to do:

sometimes when we want to calculate a route from A to B we call Google Routing API, provide A and B coordinates and receive proposed route information from Google Routing API, most importantly travel time (T) and route distance (D). what we do than is that we use T and D for dispatch decisions and display it to the drivers.

however, T and Ds that Google produces are not taking into account Bolt business specifics (ie driver behaviour, city layout features like taxi lanes etc). what we want to do is take T and Ds that Google provided and modify them with a machine learning model. This machine learning model will learn how accurate are T and Ds against actual time and distances we observe on our platform.

It seems like both a) modifying T and Ds b) using T and Ds to train internal machine learning model might contradict ToS. Hence my question can we assess whethe ToS language prohibits it.
